source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: A professor pastes a lab report into a chat session and asks it to 'grade this,' without attaching a rubric or any assignment description. The reply comes back confident and well-formatted. What does the lecture warn is the danger here?

options.text: The chat session will refuse to grade anything without more information
options.feedback: The demo shows the opposite: the session answered readily and confidently. The danger is precisely that it did not refuse, with nothing to go on.

options.text: The reply will look messy, making the missing rubric obvious right away
options.feedback: The demo's point is the reverse. The output looked polished, which is what makes the problem easy to miss rather than obvious.

options.text: The model has no idea what it is rating, and polished output can hide that
options.feedback: With no rubric or assignment description, the model is drawing only on general training about what grading looks like -- and because the result still reads well, confidence is easy to mistake for correctness.

options.text: The chat session will crash partway through generating the response
options.feedback: Nothing in the demo describes a technical failure. The danger is in the reliability of the content, not in the session failing to finish.
